extracted.intended_audience: authors and writers preparing or self-editing manuscripts
extracted.subtask_description: A practitioner checklist for authors to identify and fix common editing mistakes across fiction and nonfiction manuscripts, and to evaluate manuscript readiness. Includes both line-level errors (grammar, spelling, punctuation) and higher-level concerns (structure, citation accuracy, editing process).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammar Mistakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Wrong word use, vague pronoun references, faulty sentence structure. Even great prose collapses on grammatical errors that disrupt clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and fix incorrect word choices, unclear pronoun references, and sentence-structure faults because they impair comprehension and damage the perceived quality of writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misspelling and Typos
rubrics_metrics.description: Slip through despite spell-check. Verify language variant settings (British vs. American). The reader registers carelessness immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for typos and misspellings beyond automated spell-check; confirm the correct language variant is selected; remember that visible typos signal lack of care to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation Errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Comma misuse, apostrophe mistakes, missing/wrong hyphens, quotation errors. Punctuation controls pacing and clarity; errors corrupt both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit punctuation (commas, apostrophes, hyphens, quotations) because punctuation affects rhythm and meaning; incorrect punctuation alters pacing and can confuse readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation/Source Inaccuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: For research-backed fiction or nonfiction. Inconsistent citation style undermines credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify factual claims and references; ensure consistent citation style and accurate sourcing when the manuscript relies on research or factual material to maintain credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing Weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Repetitive words, clichés, overused adverbs, limited sentence variety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run analyses to identify repetition, clichés, adverb overuse, and lack of sentence variety; systematically eliminate these patterns to strengthen prose and voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word Omissions / Wrong Words
rubrics_metrics.description: Missing words; correctly-spelled but incorrect homonyms (their/there, lead/led, principle/principal). Use homonym reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for omitted words and incorrect-but-plausible word choices (homonyms and near-homonyms); use specialized reports/tools to surface these errors that simple spell-checks miss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural Blunders
rubrics_metrics.description: Poor organization at sentence, paragraph, scene, or manuscript levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address structural problems—weak paragraphing, muddled scene order, or overall manuscript organization—during developmental editing before moving to sentence-level edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Over-Reliance on Software
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat automated tools as aids, not substitutes: combine software reports with a professional editor or human review because tools miss nuance, voice, and higher-order issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing While Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: "Stop editing while writing. Write creatively first, and edit logically afterwards."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate creative drafting from technical editing; avoid simultaneous writing-and-editing to preserve momentum and creative flow, then perform focused edits in later passes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Over-Reliance on Self-Editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors miss their own errors consistently. The brain reads what it intended to write.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize cognitive blind spots; hire an outside editor or get fresh readers because authors typically overlook many errors in their own work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript Evaluation Metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: A manuscript can be assessed for grammar correctness; spelling/typo density; punctuation precision; citation accuracy (where applicable); word repetition rate, cliché count, adverb count, sentence variety; word omission / homonym error count; structural coherence at multiple scales; evidence of professional editing pass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use quantitative and qualitative measures—error densities, counts (repetitions, clichés, adverbs), and multi-scale structural checks—to evaluate readiness. Check for signs that a professional editing pass has occurred (consistent style, few surface errors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing Process Order
rubrics_metrics.description: The recommended order: 1) Developmental editing (structure, character, plot), 2) Line editing (sentence-level), 3) Copy editing (grammar, punctuation, consistency), 4) Proofreading (final typo sweep).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow this staged workflow: skip or reorder stages and you risk predictable failures (fixing surface issues before core structural problems leads to wasted effort and persistent defects).
